name: Brow thread lift

lead: A brow thread lift uses threads under the skin to raise the outer part of the eyebrow, offered as a less invasive alternative to a surgical brow lift.
Sources reviewed contain no completed trials. A registered study is planned to test how long the effect lasts.

paras: Threads are anchored in the brow and forehead tissue to hold the brow tail higher. Surgical lifts instead reposition tissue through incisions, and botulinum toxin raises the brow by relaxing opposing muscles [1].
Specific complication rates for brow threads were not found. Brow lifts in general carry risks such as infection, bleeding and numbness [1].

lead: A brow thread lift is a minimally invasive procedure in which threads are placed under the skin to suspend and raise the tail of the eyebrow. It is offered as an alternative to surgical brow lifts, which Wikipedia describes as procedures to raise drooping brows, with types including endoscopic, coronal and direct approaches, and non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin [1].

Published evidence is limited. One registered trial, not yet recruiting as of its listing, plans to examine whether upper blepharoplasty with ligament release improves the durability of thread-assisted brow suspension [2]. No completed clinical studies were found in the material reviewed.
infobox: One registered trial, not yet recruiting [2]

paras: Thread-assisted brow suspension uses sutures or threads to hold the brow in a higher position without the incisions of an endoscopic or coronal lift. Surgical brow lifts, by comparison, include endoscopic lifts through small incisions, coronal lifts across the scalp, and direct, mid-forehead and temporal approaches [1].

Botulinum toxin injections can raise the brow temporarily and are repeated every four to six months, according to Wikipedia [1]. The same article notes that absorbable Endotine implants have been used in surgical lifts [1].

A registered interventional trial (NCT07879456) with a planned 90 participants will assess durability of thread-assisted brow suspension combined with ligament release during upper blepharoplasty, in people with brow ptosis and dermatochalasis; it is listed as not yet recruiting [2]. No results were found.
